subject: Cognitive Science
title: Unconscious Decision Making
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Unconscious Decision Making.

hook.text: In Libet's experiment, the brain showed readiness to act 350 milliseconds before the person 'decided' to move.

buildup.text: The conscious feeling of deciding came after the brain had already committed. Decision preceded awareness.

discovery.text: Dijksterhuis found that for complex choices—like picking a car—unconscious thought outperforms analysis.

twist.text: But for simple choices with few variables, conscious deliberation is better. Complexity determines the tool.

climax.text: Much of what you call intuition is your brain running a massive parallel process you can't observe.

punchline.text: Sometimes the best decision is the one you didn't think about.

quiz.question: What did Libet's experiment reveal?
options: The brain is too slow for decisions
